structured_output.conclusion: The Atrium litigation is no longer a contingent risk. It is a settled, fixed cash obligation: $2.0M due in the rest of 2024, plus $0.6M on a second supplier settlement (VitBest), against about $2.0M of reported cash on Aug 12, 2024. Whether the requested $250k/6m advance ($265,000 total, ~$44,167 a month) can be repaid from cash on hand depends on how much of these 2024 settlement amounts was already paid by Aug 12 and when the rest falls due. If they are largely unpaid, $0.8–0.9M must come from H2 operating cash flow or refinancing before the illustrative $200k reserve and any installment are covered. In that case the 3-month offer is the most exposed and the $100k/6m offer the least. If about 35% or more is already paid, the settlements do not constrain the requested offer. The existing WebBank/Shopify loan stays under its own contract logic (25% of daily sales, with a 30% minimum in the first six months). No lending action taken; no default probability inferred from the litigation.
